papers.title: Integrating large language models for automated structural analysis
papers.abstract: Automated analysis for engineering structures offers considerable potential for boosting efficiency by minimizing repetitive tasks. Although AI-driven methods are increasingly common, no systematic framework yet leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) for automatic structural analysis. This paper proposes a framework that employs domain-specific prompt design and in-context learning strategies to enhance LLM problem-solving capabilities and generative stability, enabling fully automated structural analysis from descriptive text to model outputs. A small-scale benchmark dataset consisting of 20 structural analysis word problems (SAWPs) is also introduced to evaluate the performance of different LLMs within the proposed framework. The results demonstrate that the proposed approach can increase the level of automation in solving SAWPs compared with traditional methods. Quantitatively, the framework built on GPT-5.4 and GPT-4o both achieved 100% accuracy, outperforming GPT-4 (85%), Gemini 1.5 Pro (80%), and Llama-3.3 (30%) on the test examples. Furthermore, integrating domain-specific instructions enhanced performance by 30% on problems with asymmetrical structural configurations.

papers.title: Modeling enablers for circular economy implementation in the construction and demolition sector: a multi-method integrated approach
papers.abstract: Purpose This study identifies, prioritizes, hierarchically models, and validates the enablers that can support circular economy (CE) implementation in construction and demolition waste management (CDWM). Beyond compiling a context-specific list of enablers, the study explains how organizational, regulatory, financial, and technological conditions combine to shape CE implementation pathways in a rapidly developing construction market. Design/methodology/approach Thirty practical CE enablers were identified through expert-driven open-ended surveys conducted with UAE construction and demolition stakeholders. Total Interpretive Structural Modeling (TISM) was used to build a multi-level hierarchical structure of inter-enabler relationships. Fuzzy MICMAC analysis then classified the enablers according to their driving and dependence power. Finally, Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was employed as a complementary validation step to examine whether the broader level-wise structure implied by the TISM hierarchy was supported statistically in covariance terms. Findings The results show that foundational enablers such as top management support, training programmes, clear CE guidelines and objectives, adequate financial resources, awareness-building initiatives, and a credible regulatory environment form the base of successful CE implementation in CDWM. The hierarchical structure suggests that higher-order implementation outcomes depend on earlier investments in organizational readiness, capability development and institutional support. Fuzzy MICMAC further indicates that the most influential enablers possess high driving power, while SEM provides supporting evidence for the overall level-based structure of the model. The study also proposes a phased implementation logic, indicative resource requirements, and performance indicators that can support managerial operationalization. Originality/value The study contributes an integrated TISM-Fuzzy MICMAC-SEM framework for modelling CE enablers in CDWM and applies it in the underexplored UAE context. It extends the CE-enabler literature by interpreting the hierarchical structure through institutional theory and organizational change perspectives, thereby explaining why some enablers act as foundational conditions while others emerge as dependent implementation outcomes. The paper also strengthens practical relevance by translating the model into a staged implementation roadmap.

papers.title: Evaluating Left-Turn Conflicts under Permissive Phases Using Trajectory Data: A Comparison of Circular Green and Flashing Yellow Arrow
papers.journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering Part A Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Left-turn maneuvers at signalized intersections pose significant safety challenges, particularly under permissive phasing, where drivers are required to judge gaps in opposing traffic. To assess the safety implications of novel signal technologies such as the flashing yellow arrow (FYA), this study examines left-turn conflicts using high-resolution vehicle trajectory data collected at a representative signalized intersection in Tucson, AZ. Specifically, we compare the traditional circular green (CG) indications and FYA within the permissive phase of protected-permissive left-turn signal operations. Safety performance functions are developed with postencroachment time (PET) serving as a surrogate safety measure to quantify traffic conflicts. Conflict frequency is modeled using zero-inflated negative binomial regression to address overdispersion and excess zeros in the data. The results indicate that FYA is associated with a statistically significant reduction in PET-based conflicts compared with CG. While lower left-turn speeds and higher conflicting volumes are consistently correlated with increased conflict frequency under both indications, the effect of opposing-vehicle speed differs between them. Specifically, higher opposing speeds are associated with more frequent conflicts under CG but fewer conflicts under FYA, reflecting distinct driver adaptations to the two signal indications. Behavioral analysis reveals that FYA is associated with milder acceleration and more moderate deceleration during left-turn maneuvers, suggesting more cautious driver behavior. These findings highlight the importance of incorporating signal indication type, geometric design, and traffic dynamics into left-turn safety evaluations. From a practical standpoint, the findings suggest potential safety benefits of FYA and offer actionable insights for traffic engineers aiming to improve intersection safety through signal design and operational refinements.

papers.title: Progress in assessing wind loads on roof-mounted solar panels: Research and standards
papers.journal: Journal of Wind Engineering and Industrial Aerodynamics
papers.abstract: This paper provides a comprehensive review of existing literature and current wind code and standard provisions related to wind effects on roof-mounted photovoltaic systems, with particular emphasis on tilted PV arrays installed on flat or nearly flat roofs, which form the basis of most current design provisions. While significant progress has been made in understanding wind-induced loads on solar structures, variations in experimental setups and modeling considerations have resulted in inconsistent findings. The study examines national codes and standards, including ASCE/SEI 7 (2022), AS/NZS 1170.2 (2021), NBCC (2020), JIS C 8955 (2017) and SEAOC PV2 (2017) provisions, identifying gaps and differences in addressing the specific practical needs of solar-attached systems. An experimental investigation is presented to quantify the influence of geometric scale on extreme peak force coefficients for tilted rooftop PV arrays. The results show that large-scale models may significantly underestimate or overestimate wind peak pressures depending on PV module location within the array. Conservative amplification factors are proposed to account for geometric scale effects in wind tunnel tests employing enlarged-scale models, thereby reducing potential underestimation of extreme peak force coefficients. Finally, the paper identifies key research gaps and offers insights for future research directions and potential updates to wind codes and standards to advance their applicability for roof-mounted photovoltaic systems.

papers.title: Design and comparative assessment of the mooring system for the deepwater artificial seabed in internal solitary waves
papers.abstract: The Deepwater Artificial Seabed (DAS), a novel submerged floating structure for offshore oil production, mitigates the direct impact of harsh sea surface conditions but faces severe challenges from large-amplitude internal solitary waves (ISWs) in the South China Sea. The mooring system may either fail to constrain platform displacement due to insufficient tension or suffer structural damage from impact loads induced by excessive stiffness. This study seeks to determine the optimal mooring configuration for the DAS in ISWs. Three patterns are proposed, including a pure taut mooring and two hybrid systems with buoys or clump weights. A nonlinear coupled dynamic analysis method, experimentally validated is developed to investigate the dynamic response of the DAS under different mooring configurations. To quantify the influence of ISW amplitudes on system performance, a sensitivity analysis is conducted. Results demonstrate that the vertically arranged pure taut mooring system exhibits comprehensive advantages over the tested hybrid configurations, characterized by minimal heave motion fluctuations, stable restoring forces, and a simple structural layout. This framework offers a practical reference for mooring design and performance evaluation of submerged floating structures in ISWs.

papers.title: Modified bauxite residue blended cements – The effects of Na- and Al-rich pozzolans on phase assemblage and pore solution composition
papers.abstract: Co-calcination, vitrification and reductive smelting transforms bauxite residues (BR) into reactive SCMs. This study investigates the impact of these treatments by comparing activated BR blended cements (10–50 wt% SCM) to: (1) evaluate SCM contribution to early hydration, (2) understand late-age microstructure, (3) detect internal durability issues and (4) identify promising binder concepts. Techniques like QXRD, isothermal calorimetry or ICP-OES were used to assess the systems early- and late-age properties. Our results link early-age properties to the mineralogy of the SCMs Na-bearing phases, while the pozzolanic reactivity correlates with bulk chemistry. 30 wt% Co-calcined/vitrified BR blends form a C-A-S-H dominated, aluminate hydrate-rich microstructure similar to LC 3 systems with Na and Fe enriched AFm and C-A-S-H phases. Hydrogarnet or strätlingite precipitation were observed in the most aluminate-rich blended systems. Ternary binders with 30 wt% co-calcined or 30–50 wt% vitrified BR were identified as promising low-clinker systems.

papers.title: Tapping into the Potential of Construction Technologies to Increase the Participation of Women in the Construction Industry
papers.journal: Journal of Construction Engineering and Management
papers.abstract: Abstract Women remain significantly underrepresented in the construction sector, a pattern shaped by persistent structural and cultural barriers. Although digital transformation is reshaping the industry, the potential of adopting technologies to alleviate these gender-related challenges has been largely overlooked. Addressing this critical gap, this study examines how Construction 4.0 innovations can advance gender equity by enhancing women’s participation and empowerment within the construction industry. By employing a Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA)-guided systematic literature review of 169 articles, the research identifies 29 technologies deployed across 26 construction tasks. These technologies are categorized as either enabling (supporting women to overcome physical barriers) or enhancing (facilitating women’s advancement in technical and leadership roles). The study adopts a sociomaterial theoretical lens, emphasizing that technology and social structures are coconstitutive. The study posits that digital tools can reinforce or challenge existing gendered divisions of labor depending on how they are embedded within workplace cultures and power relations. These technologies are further analyzed across three job role categories: on-site, off-site, and fluid roles with the most cited technologies being building information modeling (BIM) (63 mentions); augmented, virtual, or mixed reality (AR/VR/MR) (37 mentions); and smart robots (26 mentions). Crucially, the findings reveal that technology’s impact is not automatic; rather, its potential to disrupt exclusionary norms and promote gender equity depends on intentional integration with organizational policies and practices. Implications include investing in inclusive technology training, gender-sensitive design and deployment, and analytics for monitoring diversity, alongside policy incentives that align adoption with organizational change. Future research is needed to empirically test the enabling versus enhancing effects across the job roles and evaluate the longitudinal outcomes of technology in the industry.

papers.title: BIM-integrated labour productivity measurement: a systematic review
papers.abstract: Purpose Building information modelling (BIM) has the potential to reduce labour intensity in labour productivity (LP) measurement, especially through automated data collection. However, the integration of BIM with LP measurement has not yet been systematically studied. This article aims to examine the knowledge gaps and explore future research directions on BIM-integrated LP measurement through a systematic literature review. Design/methodology/approach Publications retrieved from Scopus and Google Scholar in January 2025 were filtered, with 31 selected for in-depth review and analysed using scientometric and content analysis techniques. Content analysis was guided by a dialectical systems approach covering the concept, methodology and value aspects. Findings The review specifically addresses four research questions aligned with three dimensions of the dialectical systems approach. Based on the status quo of the literature, a framework is proposed that identifies seven knowledge gaps and nine future research directions. Key knowledge gaps include being limited to data collection, the need for manual input and being confined to 3D/4D BIM. Main future directions include exploring BIM for different stages, developing techniques to enhance automation and utilising additional BIM dimensions for LP measurement. Originality/value By employing a dialectical systems approach, this study offered a novel perspective on evaluating BIM-integrated LP measurement. The findings contribute to the knowledge domain by examining the knowledge gaps in BIM-integrated LP measurement with regard to the concept, methodology and value. In additions, the findings can act as a catalyst for advancing research in the identified future directions.

papers.title: Design and application of forces testing for TBM disc cutter in indoor experiment
papers.abstract: To enhance cutting system’s stiffness of linear cutting machine and obtain reliable rock breaking forces of disc cutter, this study proposes a strain-gauge-based measurement method in three bridge circuits attached in a column-frame type cutter holder. By rationally arranging strain gauges on its four columns to form three independent full bridge circuits, the normal, rolling, and side forces on disc cutter are able to be measured separately. The finite element analysis confirms the sufficient strength and high rigidity of the cutter holder and guides the optimal placement of strain gauges. Furthermore, the mapping relationships between the three-directional rock breaking forces and the output strains from three bridge circuits are determined with the calibration experiments. Finally, cutting tests on granite under different cutting parameters are performed and testing results are compared with CSM model results. It demonstrates that this method can effectively measure dynamic rock breaking force signals. Meanwhile, it reveals that the rock breaking forces measured by this method, particularly under larger penetration depths, are significantly larger than those obtained by the CSM model since the cutting system in the experiments has sufficient stiffness. The proposed method can provide accurate and reliable force data for the design of the cutter and the entire TBM machine.

papers.title: A kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition for short-term prediction of ship manoeuvring in ambient currents
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of vessel manoeuvring dynamics is essential for ensuring navigational safety in the transition toward maritime autonomy. In this study, a kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel-DMD) approach is developed to model and predict vessel manoeuvring dynamics. The vessel motion is represented using a state formulation consisting of position and resultant speed, and the Hankel-DMD method, together with a component-wise normalisation of the position states, is used to extract the modes governing the system dynamics. To improve the physical consistency of the prediction, a kinematic constraint linking vessel position and speed is incorporated as a post-processing reconstruction step. The developed approach is examined using the data generated from a physics-based Maneuvering Modelling Group (MMG) manoeuvring model for an azimuth thruster-equipped tug. Three cases are considered, including manoeuvring in calm water, in the presence of ambient current along the X -direction (following), and current along the Y -direction (cross). Quantitative error metrics show that the kinematically-constrained reconstruction reduces the trajectory RMSE by 71% in calm water (from 1.09 m to 0.31 m) and by 60% for the following current (from 7.31 m to 2.90 m). For the cross current, however, the XY-normalised pure Hankel-DMD prediction achieves the slightly lower RMSE (1.34 m versus 2.80 m for the constrained reconstruction), indicating that the benefit of the kinematic constraint is scenario-dependent. These findings demonstrate that incorporating a kinematic constraint can improve the robustness of data-driven vessel trajectory prediction, although its benefit is case-dependent under environmental disturbances.

papers.title: From Point Clouds to IFC-Compliant BIM: A Pipeline for Geometric Modeling of Arch Dam Bodies
papers.journal: Journal of Computing in Civil Engineering
papers.abstract: Abstract Dams are vital infrastructure for water resource management, flood control and hydropower generation, yet their long-term safety is increasingly challenged by aging structures and limited monitoring practices. As-built building information modeling (BIM) provides precise digital representations of existing conditions and supports life cycle management. However, conventional BIM pipelines, largely developed for buildings and standardized infrastructure, are not well-suited to hydraulic structures with highly customized geometries such as arch dams. To address this limitation, an Industry Foundation Class (IFC)-compliant BIM approach for geometric modeling of arch dam bodies using point cloud data is proposed. First, IFC-compliant templates are primarily designed for dam bodies, enabling standardized and expressive digital modeling of dam structures. A reconstruction pipeline is then proposed for geometric modeling of the dam body from unstructured point cloud data, integrating semantic segmentation with parametric geometric modeling techniques. The effectiveness of the proposed pipeline is demonstrated through a case study on a masonry arch dam, where point clouds captured by mobile laser scanning are processed to generate IFC-compliant BIM models. Results indicated that the method enables accurate reconstruction of complex dam geometries while ensuring interoperability within the BIM environment.
